rootCause.mechanism: Notification Stop invalidated the generation and stopped the foreground service. When the Activity binding ended, onDestroy called ttsExecutor.shutdownNow() and immediately called OfflineTts.release() while the single worker was still inside OfflineTts.generateWithCallback. release destroyed ONNX Runtime synchronization objects; the worker later re-entered a destroyed pthread mutex.
rootCause.nativeEvidence: FORTIFY: pthread_mutex_lock called on a destroyed mutex; kokoro-tts-runt crash at libonnxruntime.so via OfflineTts.generateWithCallbackImpl; SIGABRT; ApplicationExitInfo reason=5 APP CRASH(NATIVE), status=6.
rootCause.whyShutdownNowWasInsufficient: An ExecutorService interrupt does not synchronously quiesce JNI work. shutdownNow() returns before the native inference call has unwound.

fix.contract: NativeInferenceLifecycle serializes inference ownership against native teardown. Release is immediate only when no inference is active; otherwise the finishing worker owns release. No new inference may begin after release is requested.
serviceIntegration: Reserve inference ownership before queueing the TTS worker.
Check generation before creating native TTS and again before generateWithCallback.
Finish inference ownership in the worker finally block.
Replace onDestroy shutdownNow()-then-release with executor.shutdown(), a release request, and deferred release after the worker unwinds.
Apply the same safe release helper to cancel teardown.

newContracts: release is deferred until the in-flight inference finishes
a worker cannot start using native objects after release was requested
release is immediate when no inference is active and cannot happen twice
